page: Microsoft Azure FX64mds_v2 is a memory-intensive virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. The system is equipped with 1344.0 GB of RAM, yielding 21.0 GB of memory per core. Local storage is provided by a 3780 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance is Premium Storage capable. The CPU architecture is x86_64, supporting advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for deep learning and matrix operations.

In benchmark evaluations, the FX64mds_v2 demonstrates top-tier performance in memory bandwidth, reaching 392.4 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 170.98 GB/sec for large-block write operations. Database operations are highly efficient, with PassMark database benchmarks scoring in the top tier at 37,190.82 and Redis SET operations achieving 95.28 million operations per second. Multi-core CPU performance is strong, as evidenced by a stress-ng multi-core score of 70,926.61 and a PassMark CPU physics score of 15,470.12, which falls into the top tier. Single-core performance remains average to strong, with Geekbench single-core scoring 2095.0.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the FX64mds_v2 offers high resource density by combining massive memory capacity with high-frequency dedicated compute cores and fast local NVMe storage. This configuration minimizes the need for multi-node clustering for large datasets, optimizing licensing and architectural overhead. The instance is suited for memory-intensive workloads, large-scale relational databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, and data-intensive applications requiring high-speed local scratch space. It also supports moderate machine learning inference workloads, processing 7B parameter model prompts at 292.5 tokens per second.
